analyst_view.overall: Early view: Villa are 10th and conceded four at Old Trafford, with Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri out, and they host Galatasaray in the Champions League on 24 November. Everton under David Moyes are sixth after wins at Newcastle and at home to Coventry, driven by Thierno Barry's 10 league goals. A compact Everton against a leaky Villa defence is the key contrast.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Villa have conceded 17 in 10 and let in four goals at Manchester United, while Barry scores almost every week with headers from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's crosses. Moyes' sides are tight, but Villa's defence looks the weaker part of this match.

corners.text: The site has 10.4 corners. I agree: Villa will have more of the ball at home, and Everton work it wide for crosses toward Barry, which keeps corners coming at both ends. Nothing points far from the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, 2.8 for Everton. I agree: Moyes' Everton defend physically and will foul to stop Villa breaks, and Unai Emery's side has been on edge after the 4-4 draw. Around four or five looks right.

shots.text: The site has 28.3 shots. I lean lower: Everton under Moyes keep a low block and limit chances (only 10 conceded in 10), and their own attack is built on a few crosses rather than volume. A mid-20s total fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I agree: Villa's attack with Nicolas Jackson and Alysson is in form after four goals at Old Trafford, and Barry turns chances into shots on target. No clear reason to move.
